newsitem.title: USA: Angeion says not bound by arbitration decision.
newsitem.headline: Angeion says not bound by arbitration decision.

text.p: Angeion Corp said it is not bound by a decision that gave Medtronic Inc access to a specific group of defibrillator patents held by Angeion.
"Angeion did not participate in this arbitration and is not bound by this decision," said Whitney McFarlin, Angeion chairman and president, in a statement.
The statement was issued Tuesday in response to a recent arbitration decision awarded to Medtronic against St. Jude Medical.
Shares of Angeion were trading down one to 2-7/8.

In a dispute between Medtronic and St. Jude Medical, an arbitrator found that Medtronic had royalty-free rights to some of Angeion's early patents as a result of a pre-existing 1992 licensing agreement. St. Jude has claimed rights relating to these Angeion patents on the basis of a 1993 licensing agreement between Angeion and Pacesetter, which was purchased by St. Jude in 1995.
When Angeion signed its licensing agreement with Pacesetter, Pacesetter allegedly did not disclose specifics of the 1992 accord between St. Jude and Medtronic, Angeion said.
Angeion said it was not a party to this arbitration, and therefore, is not bound by this decision.

"We anticipated several outcomes, including this one, and we have begun to implement a strategy to deal with it. The patents at issue are a minority of Angeion's patent portfolio, and St. Jude did not have the right to license these patents royalty-free to Medtronic," he said.
Angeion said it will vigorously defend its intellectual property rights and "will pursue resolution of this matter through negotiation or other appropriate forums," he said.
Angeion designs, develops and makes medical devices to treat irregular heartbeats.
